pages.title: An Anchor That Always Comes Back
pages.text: Minamitsu's anchor is a diamond pickaxe that can also be thrown. Hold the selection key to open its mode wheel (X by default): the mode decides what a throw does, and the hotbar icon shows it. Only the two storm throws cost spiritual power.

$(bold)Destroy$()$(br)An empty left click throws the anchor: a creature takes the hit and the anchor flies back to your hand, while a block hit breaks nothing and the anchor simply returns; mining still works as usual. Left-clicking a creature swings the anchor instead of a normal attack, hurting everything within 3 blocks of it. Right click is a charge: hold it for 1–2 seconds, then release to throw an anchor that breaks blocks and damages creatures in a sphere of 3–4 blocks around the impact — the longer the charge, the wider the blast.$(br2)$(bold)Voyage$()$(br)An empty left click grabs a creature and drags it to you. Right click throws the anchor into a wall: if it hits a block it stays stuck there, pulls you over and holds you; right click to retrieve it, or sneak to let go. A throw that hits nothing pulls you from its furthest point and then returns.

$(bold)Storm$()$(br)Left click throws one unbound anchor that deals area damage on impact, at 5 spiritual power. Right click is a charge: hold it for one second while a ring of water spirals in, then the anchor releases itself and calls down a rain of anchors on every enemy that can see you or is hunting you within 32 blocks, at 20 spiritual power.$(br2)$(bold)Storm danmaku$()$(br)A storm anchor always takes the water-anchor form: it sheds a falling danmaku every tick along its flight and bursts into a spray of danmaku when it lands.

$(bold)One anchor at a time$()$(br)While the anchor is out, the hand looks empty and refuses another throw. A stuck Voyage anchor waits for you: right click within 3 blocks to call it home, or from farther away to be pulled in again.$(br2)$(bold)The power pool$()$(br)A Jizo will trade one experience level for spiritual power stored in the anchor. Without it the storm throws refuse to fire.
